exposure: formal education level (lack of formal education)
antenatal care (no antenatal care or antenatal care in an informal healthcare setting)
cohort: Pregnant women diagnosed with obstructed labour during childbirth who subsequently underwent an emergency caesarean section in 54 referral-level hospitals across Nigeria between 1 September 2019 and 31 August 2020.
finding: Women under 20 years, who lacked formal education, were unemployed, were nulliparous, did not receive antenatal care, or received antenatal care in an informal healthcare setting were significantly more likely to experience obstructed labour, and ineffective referral systems contributed to maternal death.
